business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Oversized Furniture and Home Decor

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid bijural regime: Quebec private law follows the civil law tradition (Civil Code of Quebec), while federal and public law follow the common law tradition; federal state with concurrent provincial corporate jurisdiction (source metadata legal_system_type: Federal_State).
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CUSMA (Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement) - investment and digital trade protections
CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement) - investment protection
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force 1 October 2014)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended by the 2007 Protocol (DTAA applicable to Quebec)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Implementing Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent BEPS (MLI) and Inclusive Framework Pillar Two
Global Affairs Canada network of 90+ active DTAAs extended to Quebec by provincial accession agreements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (ALPE), CQLR c P-44.1; Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, s. 2.4 (register of members); An Act respecting the communication of information relating to beneficial owners of enterprises, SQ 2023, c. 28, implementing a beneficial-ownership register at the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec in force progressively from 2024 to 2025. Canada (federal): Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), SC 2000, c 17, including ss. 9.6 and 9.7 (compliance program and FINTRAC registration); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Divisions I.2 and II.3 (freezing, seizure and forfeiture); United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky Act), SC 2017, c 21; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss. 21.1-21.4 (custody and access to information about persons with significant control), as amended by the Budget Implementation Act, 2023; FINTRAC Guidance on politically exposed persons; Revenu Quebec anti-money-laundering coordination under the Financial Administration Act, CQLR c A-6.01.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - The Quebec beneficial-ownership register (established under SQ 2023, c. 28) is accessible to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, Revenu Quebec, FINTRAC, tax authorities and law-enforcement agencies for prescribed purposes; no general public search engine access during Stage 1. The QBCA register of members remains physically inspectable at the registered office, but the persons-with-significant-control data fields are restricted to authorized authorities and accredited due-diligence actors.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) - QBCA form executed by the incorporator, optionally in notarial form
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator; if notarial form, a notary enrolled with the Chambre des notaires du Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Filed electronically with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; no apostille required for domestic Quebec filing; where the instrument is used abroad, authentication by Hague Apostille issued by Global Affairs Canada (Convention in force for Canada on 11 January 2024).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Name Reservation Certificate (Avis de reservation de nom)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for filing in Quebec; a certified copy may be apostilled by Global Affairs Canada when presented to a foreign bank, payment processor or corporate registry.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Register Extract and Attestation of Persons with Significant Control (attestation concernant les beneficiaires effectifs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary of the pre-incorporation entity, attested by a Quebec notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation plus Hague Apostille through Global Affairs Canada for foreign corporate-bank onboarding, Stripe KYB, Affirm BNPL merchant underwriting and any ADR in a non-Hague state; consular legalization required only for states outside the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Compliance / Enterprise Extract (Attestation de conformite - extrait du registre des entreprises)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by Global Affairs Canada (sole competent authority for Canada since 11 January 2024); consular legalization is reserved for jurisdictions not party to the Hague Apostille Convention.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening against: (i) Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List and implementing regulations under SEMA; (ii) United Nations Security Council consolidated list as implemented under the United Nations Act; (iii) the Canada Magnitsky Act list; (iv) the OFAC SDN list where USD clearing rails are used through Stripe; and (v) domestic sanctions under the Criminal Code. FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons and Heads of International Organizations obligations (PCMLTFA Regulations, ss. 1 and 7.1) require identity verification, ongoing transaction monitoring and enhanced due diligence for foreign and domestic PEPs, close associates and family members. CDD/EDD events are triggered at incorporation, at bank or payment-rail onboarding (Stripe and BNPL partner Affirm apply independent KYB/KYC), and at every change of significant control; screening records are retained for a minimum of 5 years in accordance with PCMLTFA record-keeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - online enterprise register and name reservation service (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; NEQ issuance through the same portal); optional NUANS database search through Corporations Canada (https://www.ic.gc.ca) if the registration contemplates any federal CBCA designation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11, s. 31 et seq.) and ALPE, the registered corporate name must be in French as the legal name; an English or other non-French version may only be used as an unofficial stylized form after the French registration is completed. No arbitrary phonetic transliteration is permitted; the name must respect French syntax, accents and punctuation and must be pronounceable in French. Where the name contains a foreign trademark or proper name, a French descriptive complement (for example Groupe, Les Services, Mobilier) must be added. Numerals or symbols that render the name non-pronounceable in French are rejected; the e-commerce storefront, invoices and public signage must display the French legal name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque (requires OSFI or Autorite des marches financiers authorization under the Bank Act and Quebec deposit institution legislation)
Securities / Courtier / Valeurs mobilieres (AMF registration required)
University / Universite / College / CEGEP (ministerial designation required)
Engineer / Ingenieur (protected title under the Quebec Engineers Act)
Architect / Architecte (protected title under the Architects Act)
Notary / Notaire (reserved to members of the Chambre des notaires du Quebec)
Barrister / Solicitor / Avocat (reserved to members of the Barreau du Quebec)
Accountant / Comptable / CPA (reserved to the Ordre des comptables professionnels agrees)
Royal / Imperiale / Municipale / Gouvernementale (requires government consent where Crown or public authority connotation arises)
Quebec / Canada / Canadian as dominant token (requires legal justification and may trigger ministerial review under ALPE)
National / Federal / Provincial (implies a public status not available to a private business corporation)
Names contrary to public order or decency, including offensive, obscene or misleading terms (Civil Code of Quebec, art. 9; ALPE, s. 14)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the incorporator may: (1) within 30 days of the REQ rejection notice, file an administrative review (demande de revision) under ALPE, s. 47, with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, accompanied by the corrected French name, supporting trademark consents or disclaimers, and the prescribed review fee of approximately CAD 45; (2) on administrative dismissal, appeal to the Court of Quebec (Chambre administrative et d'appel) within 30 days of the review decision, per the Code of Civil Procedure; (3) alternatively, file a fresh online name reservation using a materially different distinctive element, provided the rejected name is not resubmitted unchanged. A previously rejected name may be reconsidered after 6 months with evidence of acquired distinctiveness, third-party consent, or removal of the objectionable token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted. QBCA s. 18 and ALPE require the registered office (siege social) to be a physical location in Quebec where service of process can be made and where the corporate records are kept available for statutory inspection. A mail-forwarding-only virtual address without an in-province physical reception is not compliant. A licensed business centre or registered-agent office located in Quebec, with physical reception, document retention and service-of-process acceptance, is compliant and appropriate for a non-storefront online furniture retailer. The REQ register must show the full street address of the registered office and not a post office box.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at less than 5% per annum for a pure e-commerce ISIC 4791 structure maintaining only a registered office in Quebec; unannounced inspections by REQ or Revenu Quebec are primarily triggered by GST/QST registration anomalies, payroll discrepancies, or public complaints. The probability rises to 15-25% within the first 24 months if a Quebec warehouse or fulfillment center is later registered, due to municipal zoning review and QST inventory controls. An on-site inspection at the incorporation stage is unusual unless suspicious beneficial-ownership patterns are detected during the UBO filing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1 (QBCA), including sections 5–9 governing constitution and articles, and sections 118–121 concerning directors and officers. The corporation must also comply with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), administered by the Ministère de l’Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of constitution (Statuts de constitution), filed with the REQ; the corporation must subsequently file its initial declaration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital or minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares are issued for consideration determined in accordance with the QBCA and the corporation’s articles and resolutions. No statutory incorporation escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation accept the subscriptions for the shares set out in the subscription agreements, issue those shares upon receipt of the agreed consideration, and record the holders in the securities register. RESOLVED that the registered office be established at the address stated in the Articles of Constitution, subject to any required notice to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed President and [Name] be appointed Secretary, each to hold office until a successor is appointed or earlier resignation or removal. RESOLVED that the officers are authorized to complete the Corporation’s registers, make required statutory filings, obtain tax and employer registrations, and take all actions necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Clear and reserve the corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), through its online business-name search and reservation services.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the proposed French and, if applicable, English name for distinctiveness and existing registrations. Apply for name reservation if desired; alternatively, incorporate under a numbered name. A NUANS report may be useful but does not replace REQ approval. No notarization is ordinarily required for a standard incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-name instruction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, amend it to address the stated conflict or use a numbered corporate name and submit a corrected application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File articles of constitution and establish the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ online business-services portal or the REQ filing channel prescribed for articles of constitution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed articles, including the corporate name, authorized share structure, restrictions, registered-office details and first-director information, together with the prescribed fee. Provide the required declarations and contact information. Use the REQ’s prescribed signing and identity-verification method; notarization is not generally required for an ordinary domestic corporation. Obtain the certificate of constitution and enterprise number after acceptance.
required_dossiers: Name reservation or name-supporting information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deficiencies identified by the REQ and resubmit through the prescribed channel. If the proposed name is the issue, amend the articles or proceed with a numbered name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete organizational actions and corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation’s board and corporate records custodian; REQ for any required public-register updates.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting or execute written resolutions to appoint officers, approve share subscriptions and issuances, adopt a registered office, authorize banking and fiscal-year arrangements, and approve required registers and records. Record issuances only after receipt of the agreed consideration. Maintain the securities register, directors’ and officers’ records, minutes, and beneficial-ownership information as required by law.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution and filed articles
Share subscription agreements and evidence of consideration
Securities register and corporate minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Adopt corrective resolutions and update corporate records promptly. File any necessary correction or change notice with the REQ and retain supporting resolutions and evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the initial declaration and complete tax registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ online business-services portal; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec for applicable tax accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial declaration within the statutory period, generally 60 days after registration, and disclose required directors, addresses, activities, and ultimate beneficiaries. Obtain or confirm the business number and register for GST/HST, Quebec sales tax, payroll, and other accounts when legally required. Verify any applicable registration thresholds and effective dates before commencing taxable sales or employment.
required_dossiers: Enterprise number and certificate of constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected or incomplete declarations through the REQ portal and satisfy any late-filing fee or penalty. Correct tax registrations directly with the relevant tax authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board or manufacturing licence is ordinarily required for online retail of furniture and home décor. The REQ handles enterprise registration; municipal authorities regulate land use and premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general Quebec operating or manufacturing permit is ordinarily required solely for online retail. A municipal occupancy, zoning, or business permit may be required for a warehouse, showroom, or other physical premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-specific environmental impact assessment for online retail without a qualifying industrial or construction project. Projects listed under the Environment Quality Act and its regulations may require environmental assessment or prior ministerial authorization.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No retail-specific wastewater or VOC threshold ordinarily applies absent relevant operations or discharges. Any wastewater discharge, air emissions, hazardous materials, or regulated residual waste must comply with applicable provincial, municipal, and federal requirements; obtain required authorizations before commencing a regulated activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a warehouse or showroom, confirm municipal zoning and occupancy requirements, applicable Quebec construction and fire-safety code compliance, and any required fire inspection or certificate with the municipality or fire-service authority. Maintain workplace health and safety compliance under Quebec occupational health and safety legislation, including CNESST requirements. Structural-load inspections are required only where applicable to the premises, intended use, or authority direction.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal tax portal: www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency; in Quebec, Revenu Québec / Agence du revenu du Québec administers the GST/HST, QST (TVQ), and Quebec corporate income tax — portal: www.revenuquebec.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign or newly incorporated entity must first obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (extra-provincial registration, or federal/provincial incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act / Quebec Business Corporations Act). The federal statutory tax identifier is the 9-digit Business Number (BN). Apply through CRA online 'Register a business number' (BizReg) or Form RC1, selecting the GST/HST account and, where required, the Import/Export account. For Quebec sales tax and provincial corporate tax, register with Revenu Québec to obtain the QST file number linked to the BN/NEQ. Supporting records: certificate of incorporation or extra-provincial registration, registered office address, directors, beneficial owners, and business activity. Revenu Québec will issue a GST/HST and QST registration certificate when the registrant is not a small supplier or is otherwise required to register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A business corporation is a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Taxation Act (Quebec); it is not fiscally transparent and has no U.S.-style pass-through or check-the-box classification. Resident corporations pay federal and Quebec corporate tax on worldwide income, while non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada pay tax only on Canadian-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election for corporations; entity-level taxation is mandatory. Available statutory elections relevant to a Quebec business corporation include the Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) associated-company joint election for allocating the small business deduction, the eligible dividend designation election, the functional-currency reporting election (ITA s. 261), and non-calendar taxation-year elections in Quebec. The hybrid mismatch rules (disallowing deductions in hybrid mismatch arrangements) apply mandatorily and contain no elective safe harbour.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus Quebec QST/TVQ (Quebec Sales Tax / Taxe de vente du Québec); a value-added tax regime administered jointly by the CRA and Revenu Québec in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. The small-supplier threshold applies where the total value of taxable supplies made in Canada/Quebec in the preceding four calendar quarters does not exceed CAD 30,000. Registration is mandatory once the threshold is exceeded unless the only supplies are zero-rated; non-resident vendors making taxable supplies through Canadian fulfillment or permanent establishments may be required to register regardless. (No separate Quebec threshold: QST follows the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold.)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) e-invoicing mandate. GST/HST/QST invoices must be issued for every taxable supply and must show the supplier's BN/QST number, invoice date, vendor and purchaser names, description, tax rates, and tax charged. Electronic invoicing is permitted if records are legible and retained for six years; filing of GST/HST and QST returns is electronic through Revenu Québec's CLIC or CRA My Business Account. No government pre-approval API is required before issuing invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is zero-rated where the sale is made to a recipient outside Canada and the goods are exported by the vendor in compliance with the Zero-Rated Supplies Regulations (ETA Sch. VI, Part V), generally before possession is transferred to the recipient or within 60 days thereafter. For oversized furniture sold online to foreign customers, the vendor must ensure the goods physically leave Canada, via common carrier or direct export, and retain contemporaneous transport evidence. Services supplied to non-residents and performed wholly outside Canada are also zero-rated; QST zero-rating applies similarly under the Taxation Act and the QST regulations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration transmitted through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or CBSA-approved EDI; G13 / cargo control document
Bill of Lading and proof of delivery showing delivery outside Canada (carrier tracking, delivery confirmation)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/payment gateway records proving payment received from the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration
Sales contract or purchase order identifying the non-resident recipient
Carrier waybill and customs status records linking the shipment to the zero-rated sale

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority; the Department of Finance Canada holds policy responsibility for the currency; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises banks on prudential matters; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) enforces AML/CTF rules for CDD, EFT and currency reporting; Payments Canada operates the Lynx large-value clearing system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully freely convertible; Canada has maintained Article VIII status under the IMF and has operated without exchange controls since the repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1958. Capital account transactions (inbound equity, shareholder loans, outbound intercompany advances) and current account transactions (trade settlement, dividends, interest, royalties) require no Bank of Canada or Minister of Finance pre-authorization. Practical constraints are limited to: FINTRAC EFT reporting for each cross-border transfer equal to or above CAD 10,000; Part XIII federal withholding tax on dividend remittances (25% statutory rate, reduced to 5%-15% under a comprehensive tax treaty depending on the shareholder's jurisdiction); Quebec-specific requirements under the Taxation Act and the Quebec register of enterprises; and Investment Canada Act notification by a non-Canadian shareholder establishing a new Canadian business. Dividend and profit remittance is otherwise unrestricted; the corporation may maintain both CAD and foreign-currency ledgers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None — Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export proceeds. An online retail corporation exporting oversized furniture may retain export receipt balances in USD, EUR, or any transferable currency in a Canadian foreign-currency account, or in an authorized offshore correspondent account, provided each cross-border receipt is tracked for FINTRAC EFT thresholds and reconciled to underlying sale contracts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Corporate Account (CAD/USD multi-currency) plus Capital Escrow Account
Business Operating Account at a Caisse Desjardins with USD sub-ledger

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RBC Business Account CAD/USD with RBC US-control and escrow window
BMO Business Operating Account (CAD/USD) paired with BMO Harris cross-border wire access
CIBC Business Operating Account plus USD Account
TD Business Chequing Account plus USD Account linked to TD Bank N.A. cross-border servicing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM — ancillary use only. Canada does not issue or recognise the European-style electronic money institution (EMI) licence. Cross-border fintechs operate either as FINTRAC-registered money services businesses (MSBs) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), or as payment service providers (PSPs) registered with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), whose final compliance phase came into force during 2025. A non-resident EMI cannot lawfully maintain a deposit-taking notional account for the Quebec corporation; it may only provide payment facilitation and disbursement aggregation outside the core banking relationship. Wise Payments Canada, Payoneer, and Airwallex may support low-value supplier disbursement and employee refund flows, but cannot serve as the statutory capital escrow, tax remittance, or fiduciary settlement layer. The offshore EMI must be avoided for holding foreign parent funds because Canadian banks will require the source bank to be a supervised entity in a jurisdiction acceptable to OSFI and FINTRAC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no blanket statutory mandate requiring every director to appear physically at a Canadian branch. OSFI Guideline E-13 (Client Identification and Verification) permits identity verification based on original documents, notarised copies, dual-process video verification, and reliance on a regulated financial intermediary, provided the bank adopts risk-appropriate measures. In market practice, however, the Schedule I banks demand for a non-resident-owned Quebec e-commerce corporation: (i) at least one authorised signatory who is either a director or officer resident in Canada, or a nominated local representative; (ii) where no Canadian-resident director exists, original passports or embassy/consulate-notarised copies, plus proof of residential address dated within 6 months; (iii) the corporate registry records verified by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, including the attestation of conformity, the memorandum and articles of incorporation, and the updated Register of Directors and Beneficial Owners; (iv) a live video KYC interview or, for medium/high-risk profiles of the ultimate shareholder's jurisdiction, an in-person interview or notarised signature appointment at a Canadian consulate. Remote end-to-end onboarding is achievable only for low-risk shareholder jurisdictions and where a Quebec-based licensed accountant or corporate service provider acts as co-signatory and AML liaison.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner located in a grey-listed or high-risk jurisdiction, triggering enhanced due diligence and possible refusal of the account mandate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified group organisation chart down to each individual with 25% or greater ownership or control; attestation of conformity from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; embassy-notarised passports and proof of address; independent World-Check/IQS background screening report from the bank's provider; source of wealth file consisting of audited group financial statements, home-country bank reference letter on the sending bank letterhead, and income/tax summaries; written corporate purpose and expected settlement profile; consent to CRS/FATCA reporting; executed Quebec representation letter appointing a local AML point of contact.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingled settlement flows from payment aggregators (Stripe) and buy-now-pay-later platforms (Affirm) blocked as unexplained third-party deposits or suspected layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Payment Facilitator / Merchant of Record agreements; 12-month historical settlement statements from Stripe and Affirm proving gross settle to the entity and that the account is the sole settlement account; chargeback and refund reserve calculation with 90-day velocity report; PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance certificate; daily reconciliation procedure mapping T+2/T+3 card settlements to the operating account; e-commerce platform ownership documentation and the logistics fulfilment contract; explanation of Affirm's receivable funding model; monthly dedicated MID-to-account matching file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unstructured cross-border trade wires to overseas furniture manufacturers and oversized-freight forwarders flagged for unusual patterns or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders and supplier invoices with Incoterms 2020; commercial invoices, packing lists, and Canada Border Services Agency customs declarations for ocean/full-container-load shipments; executed warehouse and last-mile delivery contracts; pro-forma bank reference and beneficial ownership of each key non-resident supplier; trade-cycle mapping for five recent transactions; letter of indemnity and carrier release documentation for oversized non-palletised freight; FX transaction rationale where invoices are denominated in USD or EUR.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection recorded as equity versus shareholder loan mismatched against the bank's expected salary, rental, and purchase pipeline, creating red flags on source of funds and tax remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising the issuance of treasury shares or intercompany loan; capital schedule reconciling share premium and contributed surplus; executed cross-border loan agreement with arm's-length interest rate and repayment maturity; Section 18(4) Income Tax Act thin-capitalisation analysis (debt-to-equity below 1.5:1); Part XIII tax withholding analysis and any treaty certificate; source-of-funds confirmation from the remitting bank; 12-month cash-flow projection and procurement budget showing deployment of funds; commitment that any dividend or interest remittance will pass through the operating account after completion of statutory withholding.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Routing protocol: (1) the non-resident shareholder instructs its home bank to send a SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 pacs.008 credit transfer to the Quebec corporation's Capital Escrow Account at the chosen Canadian Schedule I bank, crediting CAD or a major currency; (2) remittance instructions must identify in the remittance field the exact corporate legal name, the Registraire des entreprises du Québec enterprise number (NEQ), and the words EQUITY INJECTION or INTERCOMPANY LOAN, as applicable; (3) FINTRAC EFT reporting applies to each transfer of CAD 10,000 or more; (4) an Investment Canada Act routine notification to Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) is required within 30 days when a non-Canadian shareholder establishes a new Canadian business; no pre-clearance or sensitive-sector authorisation is triggered at typical e-commerce capital levels; (5) a direct investment report to Statistics Canada (stock/flow survey) may be requested separately; (6) the bank will release the deposit from the escrow window to the operating account after matching the source, the UBO declaration, and the capitalisation minute; (7) if the equity is received in USD/EUR and Canadian-dollar capital expenditure is required, convert using a bank forward at day zero to eliminate open FX risk. Purpose-code narrative: use DIRECT INVESTMENT EQUITY TAKEOVER — NEW BUSINESS or INTRA-GROUP LOAN; never mix personal remittance purposes with corporate capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing hierarchy: (a) high-value CAD payments (suppliers, landlord, Revenu Québec, CRA) clear through Lynx (Payments Canada) for same-day finality, with batch ACH (Automated Clearing Settlement System) for payroll and recurring disbursements; (b) supplier payments in USD run as SWIFT MT103 to the bank's New York correspondent and clear over CHIPS or Fedwire; EUR payments clear through TARGET2 via a European correspondent; (c) commercial payments for procurement use documentary collection (DP/DA) or standby letters of credit issued by the Canadian bank as a payment risk instrument for non-trusted counterparties, with Incoterms 2020 governing the trade evidence; (d) card network settlement for e-commerce uses Stripe's direct acquiring capability with CAD settlement in T+2-T+3 and Affirm BNPL funding via its Canadian PSP; no exchange control permission is needed for any outbound payment; however, FINTRAC EFT records must be maintained and Part XIII withholding tax must be self-assessed on any interest or other periodic payments to non-residents (interest is generally exempt if arm's length and not participating debt under the Income Tax Act). The corporation should maintain separate USD disbursement ledgers per supplier, with a monthly reconciliation to Stripe and Affirm settlements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR forward contracts (vanilla forwards, tenor normally up to 24 months) documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the Canadian Bankers Association form with a Canadian Schedule I counterparty.
Foreign exchange swaps (FX Swaps) for temporary conversion and re-conversion of capital and operational surplus, permitted under OSFI-regulated market practice.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) matching long-term intercompany debt between CAD and USD, subject to arm's-length pricing and derivatives-law qualification, typically with the lending parent as the mirror counterparty.
Vanilla currency options (CAD call/USD put and reverse structures) for hedging forecast merchant receipt exposure from Stripe and Affirm USD settlements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic supplier-currency exposure (CNH, INR, IDR, VND) executed offshore with an approved non-resident bank desk; CAD/USD NDFs are not normally available or permitted because CAD is a fully deliverable currency.
Natural hedging through matching USD receivables with USD freight and supplier invoices; derivative utilisation is subject to a documented treasury policy restricting speculative transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ, c. P-44.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the calendar month following the month of the enterprise's registration anniversary (e.g., 15 March registration: 30 April annually)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 1 per day late penalty (approx. USD 0.74/day); continued non-filing for 1 year leads to REQ strike-off (radiation) and dissolution of the corporation, requiring reinstatement proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (federal corporate annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 12 fee (approx. USD 9) payable online; failure to file for one year permits the Director to dissolve the corporation (CBCA s. 212(1.1)) after notice; possibility of offence liability and reinstatement costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; balance-due day: 3 months after fiscal year-end for CCDP vs 2 months for others
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); arrears interest at prescribed CRA rates (approx. 8%+ annually for 2024-2025); wilful default fines up to CAD 25,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; installment/balance-due day 3 months after year-end for CCPCs (aligned with federal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty (5% + 1%/month) plus interest at prescribed Revenu Québec rates; directors' liability exposure for unremitted source deductions and unpaid corporate taxes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% + Quebec provincial 11.5% = combined headline 26.5% before preferential reductions
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction: federal 9% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; Quebec 3.2% on first CAD 500,000, subject to provincial income-phase-out rules. Additional incentives include accelerated investment allowances and clean technology tax credits where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed through CRA E-file or Revenu Quebec-approved software; CRA My Business Account portal for corporate accounts
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate return with quarterly or monthly statutory installments for tax balances
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due within six months after fiscal year-end. Balance due two months after fiscal year-end for non-CCPCs and three months after fiscal year-end for CCPCs eligible for the small business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, CRA business number, province of incorporation, fiscal year-end date, and corporate account identifiers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must use the permanent establishment address in Canada and provide foreign legal name and residence country details

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from online furniture sales, returns, allowances, and other income sources
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source income allocable to the Canadian permanent establishment; exclude foreign-source passive income not attributable to Canada

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after deducting cost of sales, logistics, warehousing, marketing, BNPL fees, and ordinary operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expense allocation must follow Section 247 and Schedule I of the T2 regulations; support with contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments for non-deductible expenses, reserves, dividends received, and loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations apply the same adjustments but must avoid deductible payments to foreign affiliates unless arm's-length pricing is proven

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 710 and Schedule 7 - Part I Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of federal tax before provincial allocation, small business deduction, investment tax credits, and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quebec provincial allocation only applies to permanent establishment income; treaty tie-breaker rules determine whether a filing is required at all

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax due plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeat failure penalty increases by 10% on top of base amounts. Arrears interest applies on unpaid balances, and additional penalties for false statements or omissions may reach 50% to 200% of tax evaded.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 - Quebec Corporate Income Tax Return filed through Revenu Quebec's secure section or approved E-file service providers
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual provincial return; installments coordinated with federal installment schedule for Quebec corporate tax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CO-17 must be filed within six months after fiscal year-end. Quebec tax balance due generally aligns with federal federal-installment deadlines, subject to provincial specific payment vouchers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), business number, registered office address, fiscal period start and end dates, and principal industry code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Quebec must indicate the permanent establishment address in Quebec and appoint a representative for service of documents

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income and adjustments, including Quebec-specific differences for meals, donations, financing costs, and BNPL transaction fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Trace revenues and expenses to the Quebec permanent establishment; support interprovincial revenue allocation with books and records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The final taxable income for provincial corporate tax after all deductions and loss carryovers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations compute this based on the share of Canadian business profits allocated to Quebec under the Quebec allocation rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II - Tax Credits and Contributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec investment tax credits, e-commerce media production credits if applicable, and refundable contribution adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are available only for qualified Quebec activities; treaty residents cannot claim credits without a Quebec permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable, installment credit carryforward, balance due, or refund claim; authorized officer signature and date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Quebec permanent establishment, the corporation must file a simplified non-resident declaration with applicable treaty-protection evidence

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Quebec late filing penalty is the greater of a fixed amount and 5% of unpaid Quebec tax plus 1% monthly up to 12 months; Quebec also imposes recurring interest on arrears and administrative penalties under the Taxation Act for failure to provide mandatory information.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder, before treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by their home tax authority and file CRA Form NR301 to claim reduced withholding at source. If the payer has already withheld 25%, the non-resident must file an income tax return or Form NR7 with the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain a refund. Treaty relief requires beneficial-ownership documentation, residence tie-breaker analysis, and compliance with Quebec contracting procedures where the payee is a Quebec-registered recipient entity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding: 25% for royalties and non-arm's-length interest. Treaty rates vary; e.g. Canada-US treaty generally reduces interest to 10% or exempts arm's-length interest, and reduces patent/copyright royalties to 10% or 0% for certain copyrights. Cross-border service fees are subject to withholding only when they constitute Canadian-source income; on-line marketplace operations must carefully classify IP royalties versus e-commerce services.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada does not impose a formal Local File or Master File filing threshold for most domestic corporations. Country-by-Country reporting is required only where consolidated group revenue exceeds CAD 750 million. Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be prepared whenever the corporation transacts with non-arm's-length non-residents, regardless of size, to avoid documentation failure penalties.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations, as applied in zero-tax jurisdictions, are not separately enacted in Canada. Instead, substance is tested through the general anti-avoidance rule, permanent establishment jurisprudence, beneficial-ownership tests in treaty claims, and gross-negligence penalties. A Quebec corporation that serves solely as a booking entity without real inventory, staff, or decision-making is exposed to treaty denial and Section 247 adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of online furniture sales, suppression of BNPL revenue, claiming fictitious warehousing expenses, or destroying sales records in e-commerce platforms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty under Section 163(2) of the Income Tax Act: 50% to 200% of tax evaded; criminal prosecution under Section 239 carries fines up to 200% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years on indictment. Quebec additional penalties apply under the Taxation Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize false filings may be personally assessed for unremitted withholding and GST/QST; fraudulent behavior pierces the corporate veil, enabling civil seizure of personal assets, travel bans through court enforcement, and imprisonment for knowing participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Quebec federal/provincial corporation solely to book Canadian income while intellectual property, logistics decisions, inventory management, and control are exercised from a tax haven or foreign principal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of full Canadian taxable income in the hands of the Quebec entity; denial of treaty benefits; application of the GAAR penalty under Section 163(2) where avoidance outweighs real economic substance; potential Part XIII withholding on recharacterized payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell company risk personal planning-penalty assessments, joint-and-several liability for taxes arising from sham structures, and criminal exposure under offshore compliance and foreign reporting penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties or management fees to related foreign entities for dynamic content, software platforms, or brand licensing beyond arm's-length values; materially under-remunerating Canadian sales function for oversized-freight logistics.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 247 transfer pricing adjustment to arm's-length amount, plus penalty of 10% of the adjusted amount in cases where documentation is deficient; compounded with interest and late-filing penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve non-arm's-length arrangements with affiliated overseas companies can be held accountable for planning penalties; if documentation is fabricated, criminal liability may arise for aiding false tax returns.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Part XIII Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to a foreign parent or foreign affiliate without withholding the statutory 25% or proper treaty-reduced rate; attempting to repatriate profits through false management fees or loan re-payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Part XIII taxes are held in trust for the Crown; failure to remit triggers full liability, interest, penalties, and fines under Sections 227 and 231 of the Income Tax Act; Quebec may assert parallel collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted withholding taxes regardless of the corporation's dissolution; tax authorities may issue civil freezes, directors' liability assessments, travel bans under enforcement orders, and refer egregious cases for criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Obligations through High-Risk Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting BNPL and card payments without adequate customer identification, suspicious-transaction monitoring, or FINTRAC reporting despite the Low_Risk_Standard tier; high-volume oversized-furniture transactions may still be monetized through untraceable refunds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; Quebec securities or financial regulation penalties where applicable; CRA can also impose unreported-gain penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers can incur personal administrative fines for willful AML non-compliance; serious money-laundering findings can lead to asset seizure, travel bans, and non-tax criminal charges.
